title: Topic 1.4: Listening for information, Oral Expression

pages.lesson:
LESSON: LISTENING FOR INFORMATION, ORAL EXPRESSION

Grade: Grade 9
Subject: GERMAN
Strand: Listening and speaking
Topic 1.4: Listening for information, Oral Expression

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Listening for information, Oral Expression. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: how old members of family are, What can you do to improve your oral expression?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify essential information from given texts
2. appreciate the role of correct language structures in oral expression

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: LISTENING FOR INFORMATION, ORAL EXPRESSION
Subject: GERMAN · Grade: Grade 9
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Listening for information, Oral Expression helps you succeed in GERMAN. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: LISTENING FOR INFORMATION, ORAL EXPRESSION
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Identify essential information from given texts

What this means
In this part you learn to identify essential information from given texts. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify essential information from given texts.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Listening for information, Oral Expression”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify essential information from given texts. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Appreciate the role of correct language structures in oral expression

What this means
In this part you learn to appreciate the role of correct language structures in oral expression. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: appreciate the role of correct language structures in oral expression.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Listening for information, Oral Expression to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can appreciate the role of correct language structures in oral expression. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Listening for information, Oral Expression is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Listening for information, Oral Expression”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: identify essential information from given texts)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Listening for information, Oral Expression to a partner. (skill: appreciate the role of correct language structures in oral expression)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Listening for information, Oral Expression to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify essential information from given texts.
3. Practise this skill: appreciate the role of correct language structures in oral expression.
4. Make one local Kenya example of Listening for information, Oral Expression from your county, market, farm, or school.
5. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Listening for information, Oral Expression: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 9 learner study Listening for information, Oral Expression?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. how old members of family are, What can you do to improve your oral expression?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Listening for information, Oral Expression means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify essential information from given texts.
5. Be able to: appreciate the role of correct language structures in oral expression.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
